notes.title: Update 1.2.2 - Steam Achievements Are On the Menu!
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, Crew Members![/p][p][/p][p]Two updates in a month - wowza! I'm very happy to bring Update 1.2.2 to y'all, a small but much requested one that finally brings Steam Achievements to the game. There are now 26 achievements to be unlocked for you completionists out there. All twenty six have been verified on our end to be acquirable, so happy hunting, y'all! Please be aware, since Steam Achievements weren't on our radar when we first released SMH, these are [u]not[/u] retro active. If you have technically completed an achievement prior to 1.2.2 (for example, finishing a character's route), you will need to do so again in order for Steam to recognize it. Just a reminder that you can quickly speed through dialogue by holding down the Left CTRL button!  [/p][p]HUGE THANKS TO [b]korytoombs/Sunflower Games[/b] FOR THEIR AMAZING WORK PUTTING TOGETHER THE PLUG-IN THAT ENABLES OUR ENGINE TO INTERACT WITH STEAM'S SDK! We never could have gotten this working without them - please consider supporting them on itch.io, and our heartfelt thanks again![/p][p]Lastly, this update also comes with a bug fix for the previously mentioned Quick Speed bug that occurred when switching between save files that were set at different campaign lengths. This issue should now be impossible reproduce, but as always - please let me know on the forums if there's any issues. [/p][p]Barring any huge changes in circumstance, this'll likely be my [i]real[/i] last update for a while. Very happy we got a chance to add these requested features. Thanks again, everybody, and HUGE welcome to the big influx of players who've picked up the game over the last month. Take care, ya wild cats![/p][p][/p][p]Elijah[/p][p][/p][p][i]Patch 1.2.2[/i][/p][p][i]Changelog:[/i][/p][p][/p][list][*][p][i]Added 26 Steam Achievements across all routes of the game[/i][/p][/*][*][p][i]Fixed a bug introduced in 1.2.1 that required players to fully exit the game if they wanted to play a normal length campaign after starting or loading into a save file set to a short campaign length[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]

notes.title: Update 1.2.1 - Shorter Playthroughs, Additional Dialogues & More
notes.notes: [p]Hello there![/p][p][/p][p]Surprise update! Just a small one - added a handful of more dialogue options, revisited the writing in a few scenes, fixed some typos, and, by request, added a campaign length option![/p][p]Upon launching a [u]new[/u] campaign, players will be prompted to choose their 'shift length' -- a Single (approx. 3-4 hour) or Double (approx. 7-8 hour) playthrough. The new abbreviated playthrough skips the prologue, the weekend heist, majority of Week II and most 'connective tissue' scenes. Additionally, a handful of scenes needed to be rewritten to introduce characters and themes like Patty that you'll need to be acquainted with for character routes that otherwise, in the abbreviated format, the player wouldn't have met yet. On the shortened campaign length, players only need to rack up a measly 4 Craveability Points to kick off a character's arc; the content and length of character arcs, including Solo, has not been edited, however - only the length of the Core Route has been adjusted. Please see the full changelog below for complete details of everything added/changed in 2.1.1.[/p][p]Just for full transparency, this update isn't reflective of a change of plans when it comes to future game updates - those are, unfortunately, still on ice. This was just a relatively quick update to knock out one of the things we promised (shorter campaign). We are still absolutely looking for a way to get Steam Achievements working - but as it stands, the VNM Engine absolutely hates Steamworks integration. If we can get it working, you can expect another li'l update.[/p][p]Please note, there is a pretty major issue specifically with changing between quick and normal speed playthroughs that just came to my attention after the update went Live. I already have several ideas of how to fix it, and will hit it with a fast patch soon as I can! Full details in the changelog. notes.title: Patch Notes for 1.2.1
notes.notes:
Hello, there!

Small update incoming, with more details in just a bit. Here's the rough and tumble changelog:

[list]
[*] Implemented ‘campaign length’ option to enable shorter playthroughs, available when starting a new game
[*] Added option to partner with the General on Week 1, Friday Morning Exam
[*] Added option to either go with Nom Nom on Friday Morning and participate in the sky fight with Samuel Wich, or skip straight to class 
[*] Added variation of Week 1, Friday Night Nightclub scene to account for if the player didn’t go with Nom Nom that morning
[*] Added dialogue choice to Week 1, Monday Morning Pre-Class scene
[*] Added dialogue choices to Week 1, Tuesday Evening Expresso scene
[*] Added dialogue choice to Week 1, Thursday Morning Lunch scene
[*] Added dialogue choice to Week 1, Friday Morning Hotel scene
[*] Added dialogue choices to Week 1, Friday Afternoon Lunch scene
[*] Substantially decreased the previously egregious length of the Week 1, Wednesday Afternoon Beach scene between Saul and Mackie 
[*] Shooting Samuel Wich with the harpoon gun now awards players +1 Craveability with Sovereign, even though he isn’t physically present (presumably he felt your actions reverberate through your Soul Bond)
[*] Substantial flow and dialogue changes to the Week 1, Wednesday Expresso scene where the player meets Siren and Bae
[*] Minor reworking of dialogue across various scenes
[*] Adjusted volume for two lowest music settings to allow for even quieter tunes 
[*] Fixed various typos
[/list]
A post with a bit more information should be live just a bit later this morning. All the love!

Elijah and Co.

notes.title: Farewell, Flavor City!
notes.notes:
Greetings, Crew Members!

Since Supersize My Heart was just a twinkle in my eye four and a half years ago, it's been an absolutely wild ride taking this game from concept all the way to release. I've been able to work with genuinely, astonishingly talented people from all around the world to bring this silly game together. Reading people's reviews and watching let's plays of the game - it's just all been absolutely phenomenal. An experience I wouldn't trade for anything. 

Sadly, the time has come to bring support for Supersize My Heart to a close. Since launch, we released several bug fix patches, a major update that (in my opinion) massively improved the game by adding dialogue options to romance routes and throughout the core experience, rewrites to scenes, and additional polish and features throughout. However, we never got around to some very important stuff - namely, an addition of shorter route lengths and sexy romance routes for Sonny and Saul as free downloadable content. Those updates will sadly not happen. 

Why? Put very, very simply: the game did not strike a chord with people, which I say with no degree of sadness or bitterness - just because y'all deserve to know the truth, and it's clearly evident anyway. As many who have followed the project since the beginning know, we had zero funding - I have funded the entirety of Supersize My Heart myself, from asset creation to QA to marketing, to the tune of about $35,000. To date, Supersize My Heart is at roughly $500 in sales.

And that is completely fine with me - I came into this project knowing how goofy and niche it was, and expecting to not make my investment back. That being said, the notable unpopularity of the game, combined with health problems in my eyes that've cropped up in the last year or so, and the fact that my position in my nine-to-five job was recently terminated - with all of these in mind, it is not possible to continue working on the game at this time. 

I say again - it's been fun. I spent a small fortune creating this game, and I do not regret it. The writing could definitely be better, the code behind the scenes is absolute spaghetti - but with the help of amazing people, I made something! Who cares if it wasn't popular. If you're reading this, I hope you go out and make something, too. You can do it! If an idiot like me can, there's no doubt in my mind you'll crush it. And if you're one of the lovely few who bought the game, played it, streamed, left a review, any of that - from the bottom of my heart: [b]thank you. [/b]

[b]Thank you, thank you, thank you.[/b]

All the best, Crew Members! Keep on cooking, and always stay zesty! Ya wild animals!

-Elijah, Jeremy, and the whole dang team

notes.title: Supersize My Heart - Update 1.2.0! Choices, Choices, Choices
notes.notes:
Heya, Crew Members!

March is here, and our first update in 2025. Many hours and over 300 Canva assets later, we've made hundreds of little changes across the course of the game that I hope improve the experience. 

The biggest of which: I added choices to all four of the character routes, and the solo route. No longer does the game become strictly kinetic as soon as you start the final arc of your playthrough. These are very similar to the choices you'll find in the Common Route - but they're not meant to provide drastic branching paths. You'll still follow the story of the route - the choices (mostly dialogue options, like you'd find in an RPG) are more meant to let you express yourself and 'flavor' your experience. That being said, there *are* a few choices you can make that might straight up [i]bump you from your route[/i] - so watch out for those!

All in all, I'm very happy with this update. I think it vastly improves the experience. If you have any questions or encounter any bugs that I missed, please hit me up via email or here in Discussions and I'll get them taken care of ASAP! 

Next update, which I'm hoping will drop next month: abbreviated playthroughs and Steam Achievements! That'll be fun - I'll actually have to do a bit of coding for once, so fingers crossed! 

All the best! 

Elijah


P.S. 

You can find the more-or-less complete change list below:

[list]
[*] Added approx. 120 choices across the five routes (Mackie, Sovereign, Kai, the General, Solo)
[*] Added 3 new choices to Common Route scenes previously missing choices
[*] Player is now directly informed via an on-screen banner when they've exited the Common Route and started their final route, whatever that happens to be for their playthrough
[*] Player is informed via a direct message and via the Employee Handbook how many Craveability points they need to romance a character (7)
[*] Craveability needed to romance a character is now standardized (7)
[*] Player is informed Monday Morning, Week 1 how to skip through dialogue (Ctrl button)
[*] 'Sauce' has been added to the Music Library
[*] Dozens of edits across all routes to remove the most egregiously cringy dialogue I could find (some was left for posterity, and because some of it I find funny)
[*] Tweaks to dialogue when meeting Sovereign and Mackie for the first time
[*] Additional dialogue added to nearly all routes to clarify previously glossed-over narrative issues 
[*] Changed New Game+ messaging so it no longer refers to the Express Route as having no player choices
[*] Various minor scene flow changes across all routes
[*] About half a dozen spelling mistakes VANQUISHED
[/list]

notes.title: What's Coming Soon - Supersize My Heart in 2025
notes.notes:
Hello again, everybody! Elijah here. 

February's been a great month for Supersize My Heart, and I seriously can't put to words how much I've enjoyed watching people play the game on YouTube and Twitch for this, the most romantic month of the year. Huge thanks to the phenomenal steamers, YouTubers and reviewers who've taken the time to check us out! It's also been great for getting feedback - and in response, I'm excited to talk about what's coming next. 

Overall, we've had positive reactions to the game - but there's a common theme that keeps emerging: that the game may be too long. Or, even, substantially too long.

Supersize My Heart seems to run most players from prologue to credits about [i]five and a half hours[/i], for a single route (with five standard routes, and a lengthy epilogue). I think we can all agree that's a little silly for what this game is. It doesn't help that until today our forum description incorrectly said a playthrough should take about [i]an hour and a half.[/i] [b]TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE[/b], we're currently working on a campaign length option that will allow players to choose, at the start of a playthrough, whether they would like to play a Standard (or Sit-Down) playthrough of 5 1/2 hours, or the abbreviated (Quick Service) playthrough of about 2 hours. The abbreviated playthrough will have shorter sequences and be missing some of the 'connecting tissue' scenes found in a regular length playthrough. We'll have more information about this in the coming weeks.

Thankfully, we haven't heard about any bugs (yet; fingers crossed) in Supersize My Heart, but we will be fixing a handful of spelling and grammar mistakes that we've noticed since our last update. Also, we'll be adding 'Sauce' to the Music Library. I'm not sure why it wasn't there before - I dropped the ball, that's on me.

And finally, we're excited to announce what I'm tentatively calling our [i]Sonny-side Up(date)[/i]. This Summer, we're bringing a new route to the game centered around everyone's infamous and up-till-now very much un-dateable starman, Sonny. As a character added post-launch, completing his route will not be necessary to unlock the Epilogue; but he will be a selectable romance partner when playing through the Epilogue. The Sonny-side Up(date) is free and will be patched into the game like previous updates. 

Huge thanks again to everyone who's taken a chance on us and checked out the game! We'll see y'all next month for Steam Visual Novel fest! 

All the best! 

Elijah
